institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city and the school.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Sciences Po made it rather easy to know any practical information upon arrival. 
Course selection and application prior to arrival were a bit more difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get any specific assistance apart from the general information provided by SciencesPo

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was very lucky to get a spot at the Cité International. I would absolutely recomend trying to get a spot here. 
I applied to the danish house in the Cité and the danish house sent me on "exchange" to the Mexican house. 
I very much enjoyed living in the Cité. Not only are many of the houses much cheaper than finding your own apartment in the city, it is also where I met most of my friends. The Cité also as great facilities (e.g. for sports) that are cheap for residents to use.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Apply to a spot in the danish house in the Cité Universitaire and do not worry if you get sent on exchange/brassage. Even if the house you end up in is not very social, you can try to contact the other Danes that are on exchange/brassage in different houses. During my semester there were ca. 20. of us living in different houses and many of us became very good friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was made difficult because UCPH had trouble submitting our spots to SciencesPo. This meant that we did not have a lot of time to register at SciencesPo.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is a registration process at SciencesPo, even after UCPH has granted you a spot. 
Here, you need to choose the specific school that you want to attend at SciencesPo. There are several. I chose PSIA (Paris school of international affairs). You have to prepare some documents and write a motivational text about why you want to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not seek any help for this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not very succesfull. As an exchange student, you get to pick your classes after all the regular students. This happens at a certain date and time where everyone sits ready at their computer and registers on a first come first serve basis. It is rather chaotic and many of the courses are already filled at this time. 
Therefore it is very important that you research different options beforehand. 

The classes I ended up taking were very interesting so it is not the end of the world if you do not get your first priority. During the first couple weeks of the semester, it may also be possible to switch some courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very prepared for course registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was overall rather similar to UCPH. Students at ScienesPo tend to have a more narrow focus in their studies. If you choose a course on a certain topic you may therefore end up having it with students who have taken many courses on the topic. You might therefore feel behind, but you will probably be just fine for your exams. 

The main difference is the assessment. Each course has at least 2 different assessments and some may have many more. You might for example be graded on an essay, mid-term, presentation and participation for one course. This increases the workload compared to UCPH, but if you are used to having a student-job besides your studies in Denmark, then the overall workload will probably not be an issue.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It depends a lot on the professor. They all do it very differently. 
Some used a lot of group discussions, others just spoke for 2 hours.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Warning failure and Surprise attack 
Social inequality across the life course 
Global inequality and sustainability 
The migration and development nexus 
Climate geopolitics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Warning failure and suprise attack --> very interesting if you are interested in intelligence. The professor was very engaging. 
Social inequality across the life course --> interesting and definitely the most chill course I had. There were ca. 5 pages of mandatory reading pr. week. 
Global inequality and sustainability --> Interesting and a very engaging professor.

questions.answer: If you get housing in the cité universitaire, you can be very lucky and end up in a house with cheap rent. My rent in the mexicna house was 460 euros pr. month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I ended up going out to eat and drink more than I had expected to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had sports and clubs avaliable but I did not really use them. I played sports in the Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an intro-week for exchange students with trips to museums etc. I did not take part in this.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the museums if you are under 26. This gives you free entry.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Maybe explore the rest of France via the fast trains. (TGV's)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Everyone at SciencesPo speak english and it is a rather internatonal environment. So this was pretty easy. 

In daily life, speaking a little bit of french definitely helps.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I ended up speaking mostly with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food and drink.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for course registration.  

The common core course are usually more chill. They are 4 ects for normal students but 6 for exchange students. You are allowed to pick 2 of these. I found that doing this decreased my workload.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having enough time to feel like you fully explored Paris.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
